findings.evidence: A joins asking rebalance_timeout_ms=6000; the round opens, A is Pending, and join publishes fold([A]) = 6 s. B joins asking 300000; plan_and_join enrols B into round.members, returns Pending, and drops the rounds lock. close_on_deadline takes the lock in that window and runs finalize_close, whose std::mem::take(&mut round.members) empties the roster while leaving entry.open installed, and which publishes nothing itself. B's publish_sync_wait then takes the lock: ready_close is None because the outcome is Pending, sync_wait::publish folds the empty open roster to None, and set_rebalance_timeout returns early on None. The stored 6 s stays. The generation closes on a 6 s backstop, so B and every follower of that generation leave the assignment barrier at MIN_SYNC_WAIT_MS with REBALANCE_IN_PROGRESS instead of the 300 s asked for, and if the leader's SyncGroup exceeds 6 s the group rebalances again rather than completing. The pre-43b21a2 unconditional max fold could not produce this. DISPOSITION (1) reopens M4: 'something a Kafka client observes' is the test verbatim, roadmap.md says so in those words, and M4.83's own row was filed blocking on the same test one commit earlier. The row is M4.87, which already exists and is open, so this finding costs no new file and this artifact's commit stays reviews-only. ⚠️ WHAT DISPOSITION 1 COSTS, said here because nothing else will say it and no gate can: dispositions 1 and 2 are exclusive, and M4.87 currently carries all of disposition 2's artefacts. Reopening means the commit that works it must also take M4.87 out of roadmap.md's 'Deferred into a later milestone' cell and out of M5.md task 22, and must rewrite backlog.md's opening clause, which says 'neither is a reopen' and is wrong at this finding's severity rather than at minor. No gate catches the half-done state: check-milestone-review.sh only checks the row exists and is open, check-milestone-handoff.sh is satisfied *because* the row sits in the Deferred cell, and m4-complete.sh reads no backlog rows -- so a next commit that flips M4's roadmap cell to complete with M4.87 still todo passes everything, M5.0 dissolves the row, and the race leaves M4 unrepaired. That is the outcome this regrade exists to prevent, reached by the route the regrade itself opened.

findings.evidence: M4.83's per-commit rounds 2 and 3 graded the race above minor, and this round first accepted that grade. review.md rule 9a floors *prose* findings at minor and does not license grading a code race minor; because it arrived at the boundary as a harvested rule-15 minor rather than as a round's finding, milestone-review/SKILL.md's disposition rule never bound on it. roadmap.md states the route rather than closing it. 39f1bc9's body records this and calls it a decision for a later commit. It stays minor because acting on it edits review.md and the milestone-review skill: nothing a client, an operator or another tenant observes, and no gate that cannot fail. What is no longer true is the cost argument this round first gave for not majoring the race itself -- that either alternative disposition would produce an enumerated uncovered commit. M4.87 already exists at HEAD and open_task_ids lists it, so a blocking finding citing it stages no new file. The minor grade bought nothing but an earlier close.
